Include: a title and HUD (level, moves), and the puzzle board with the player, one or more crates, a lever, a target/goal (and a door), walls, and a controls legend. Put strong emphasis on the visual design: a distinct identity and a board that reads as a real puzzle — careful layout, color, typography and finish. history.critique: Brief & Intent: All required elements are present (title, level/moves HUD, player, crate, lever, glow-pad target, door, walls, controls legend), but the board — the core of the brief — is clipped at the bottom: the lower wall row is cut off by the panel edge, so the puzzle does not read as a complete, bounded, solvable space. The lever→door relationship is only stated in the objective text; on the board there is no visible state link or open/closed affordance beyond a tiny 'OFF' tag. Clarity & Hierarchy: The board is the intended focal point yet sits under a large empty band at the top of its panel while overflowing at the bottom, breaking vertical rhythm and preventing the eye from landing on the puzzle. Floor vs wall contrast is too low (both near-black blue), so maze topology is hard to trace and the outer boundary is only implied by the top wall row. HUD accent colors are arbitrary — PAR and TIME share the same red, diluting meaning — and the lever icon in the field guide is nearly invisible against its chip. Visual System & Craft: Only one decorative corner bracket (top-left) is rendered, which reads as unfinished; the lever's 'OFF' label is ~6px and low contrast; the door's lock glyph is too small to read; tile bevels are inconsistent (some walls show a top highlight, others don't); sidebar icon chips have uneven contrast. history.suggestion: Prioritized plan: 1) Fix the board frame first — size tiles to fit the panel (keep ≥38px), vertically center the grid, render the full outer wall ring, and remove the dead top band (or repurpose it as a small 'LEVEL 03 — THE WORKSHOP' plate). history.critique: Brief & Intent: The brief explicitly requires walls, and the field guide even lists 'Wall — Solid stone', yet no wall tiles exist on the board — the level has no visible boundary, so the board fails the brief's core demand to 'read as a real puzzle'. The player is a glowing amber orb that reads as a light source rather than an 'Operator' character with agency. The lever-to-door dashed wire is a nice authored touch, but its mid-line node is unexplained. Clarity & Hierarchy: The two-tone checkerboard floor is ambiguous — playable floor, void, and level edge are indistinguishable, so the player cannot infer the solution space. The HUD duplicates PAR (inside the Moves card AND as its own card) and the level appears three times (header subtitle, HUD card, board pill). Critically, the board overflows the viewport and is clipped at the bottom, so the full puzzle is not visible at once — fatal for a puzzle game's main screen. Visual System & Craft: Floor tiles are muddy, low-contrast beveled squares with inconsistent lighting; the HUD accent system is inconsistent (only the first two cards have colored left bars); the board's corner brackets appear only on top; the lever toggle graphic is small and muddy; the field guide's wall icon depicts a tile type that never appears on the board, undermining the legend's credibility. Expressiveness: The 'Workshop' theme exists only in the name — the board is a generic dark-dashboard grid; the amber/teal duotone and mono type are solid, but the floor lacks material character and the crate is the only truly crafted element. Trade-offs: the checkerboard texture adds visual interest but destroys spatial readability; the long field guide is thorough but competes with the board and duplicates on-board elements; the redundant fourth HUD card wastes space that could enlarge the board.
history.suggestion: Prioritized plan: (1) Rebuild the board's spatial system first — introduce real wall tiles (riveted steel/stone blocks with a distinct material and top highlight) that bound the level, make playable floor a single consistent tone with a subtle workshop texture (worn metal plates or wood), and render out-of-bounds as a recessed near-black void; then scale the grid so the entire board fits the viewport with no scrolling, since the puzzle must be fully visible. (2) De-duplicate the HUD: keep three cards (Level, Moves with PAR beneath, Time) or repurpose the fourth as best-score/stars, apply the accent-bar system consistently across all cards, and remove the duplicate level pill or reduce it to a thin level-name banner. (4) Clarify the lever→door circuit: keep the dashed wire but animate a pulse traveling it on pull, switch the door's lock to an open state, and visually explain the mid-node as a junction/conduit; show the lever's ON state in the field guide. (5) Push the workshop identity onto the board itself — warm floor material, riveted walls, a soft vignette and ambient glow from the pad and orb — while retaining the amber/teal duotone and monospace type. (6) Finish details: corner brackets on all four board corners, a visible move tick on the counter, and a subtle last-move/hover highlight on tiles.
